source_text: Attende ergo, frater, attende, obsecro te. dicis mihi: quid me quaeris? respondeo: quia frater meus es. respondes mihi et dicis: si perii, quid me quaeris? et ego respondeo: si non perisses, non quaererem. quid me quaeris? dicis mihi: si perii, quid me quaeris? cum ego respondeam: quaero quia peristi. et quare quaero, quo fructu quaero? ut aliquando dicatur mihi: frater tuus mortuus erat et reuixit, perierat et inuentus est. respondes et dicis mihi: sed habeo sacramentum. habes, agnosco; propter hoc te quaero. magnam causam addidisti, quare diligentius te quaeram. ouis es enim de grege domini mei, cum signo errasti; ideo quaero magis, quia ipsum signum habes. quare unam ecclesiam non possidemus? unum signum habemus; quare in uno ouili non sumus? ideo te quaero, ut hoc sacramentum sit tibi in salutis adiutorium, non in damnationis testimonium. nescis quia desertor de charactere damnatur, de quo militans honoratur? ideo te quaero, ut non pereas cum signo. salutis enim signum est, si habeas salutem, si habeas caritatem. hoc enim signum salutis extra tibi inesse potest, prodesse non potest. ueni, ut prosit tibi quod habebas, non ut accipias quod habebas, sed ut prodesse tibi incipiat quod habebas et accipias quod non habebas. habebas enim signum pacis, ipsam pacem non habebas. in domo illa, id est in te, discordia habitabat et in limine titulos pacis figebat. agnosco titulos, sed quaero habitantem. lego titulum pacis: baptismus in nomine patris et filii et spiritus sancti. titulus pacis est, lego; quis habitet, quaero. fratrem meum attendo, titulum pacis agnosco. ipsum et ego habeo, intrare uolo. quid est \'intrare uolo\'? fratrem me accipe, ut simul oremus patrem. \'non tecum oro\'. tituli pacis sunt, et mihi discordia contradicit? plane laborabo adiuuante domino eicere discordiam male possidentem et introducere pacem tamquam legitimum possessorem. cum ergo discordiam excludo, pacem introduco, titulos pacis quare depono? dico plane domino meo: \'o Christe, qui es pax nostra, qui fecisti utraque unum. fac nos unum, ut recte cantemus: ecce quam bonum et quam iucundum habitare fratres in unum. introduc concordiam, pelle discordiam; introduc te ipsum in titulos tuos. tu mane, non alter possideat et de titulis tuis fallat.
thought_title: The lost sheep bearing the sign of peace
orientation: Augustine is addressing Emeritus directly, answering his objection that he should not be sought if he has perished, and explaining that the very sacrament Emeritus possesses is the reason he must be sought.
pass_a_gloss: Attend therefore, brother, attend, I beseech you. You say to me: why do you seek me? I answer: because my brother you are. You answer me and say: if I perished, why do you seek me? And I answer: if you had not perished, I would not seek [you]. Why do you seek me? You say to me: if I perished, why do you seek me? When I answer: I seek [you] because you perished. And why do I seek [you], with what fruit do I seek [you]? That at some time it may be said to me: your brother was dead and has revived, had perished and has been found. You answer and say to me: but I have the sacrament. You have [it], I acknowledge [it]; because of this I seek you. A great cause you have added, why more diligently I should seek you. A sheep you are for of the flock of my Lord, with the sign you have strayed; therefore I seek [you] more, because the very sign you have. Why one church do we not possess? One sign we have; why in one fold are we not? Therefore I seek you, that this sacrament may be to you for salvation [as] a help, not for damnation [as] a testimony. Do you not know that a deserter by the brand is condemned, by which [brand] a soldier is honored? Therefore I seek you, that you may not perish with the sign. Of salvation for a sign it is, if you have salvation, if you have charity. For this sign of salvation outside you can be in [you], be of profit cannot. Come, that it may profit you what you had, not that you receive what you had, but that it may begin to profit you what you had and [that] you receive what you did not have. You had for the sign of peace, peace itself you did not have. In that house, that is in you, discord was dwelling and on the threshold titles of peace was fixing. I acknowledge the titles, but I seek the inhabitant. I read the title of peace: baptism in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. A title of peace it is, I read [it]; who dwells, I seek. My brother I attend to, the title of peace I acknowledge. The very [title] I also have, to enter I wish. What is 'to enter I wish'? My brother receive me, that together we may pray [to] the Father. 'Not with you do I pray.' Titles of peace they are, and to me discord contradicts? Clearly I will labor with the Lord helping to cast out discord wickedly possessing and to introduce peace as [the] lawful possessor. When therefore discord I cast out, peace I introduce, the titles of peace why do I put away? I say clearly to my Lord: 'O Christ, who are our peace, who made both one. Make us one, that rightly we may sing: behold how good and how pleasant [it is] to dwell [as] brothers in one. Introduce concord, drive out discord; introduce yourself into your titles. You remain, let not another possess and by your titles deceive.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'sign of peace' for titulus pacis; the plural here refers to the inscription of baptism as a sign posted on the person.
The glossary requires 'mark' for character, the seal of baptism and ordination belonging to Christ.
The glossary requires 'deserter' for one who has left the Catholic Church.
The glossary requires 'love' for caritas, the love without which sacraments profit nothing.
In 'fecisti utraque unum' and 'fac nos unum', 'one' preserves the Pauline and Johannine sense of unity in Christ.
The glossary requires 'sign of peace' for titulus pacis, baptism as a sign of peace posted on a person.

ecce quam bonum et quam iucundum habitare fratres in unum

pass_b_english: So pay attention, brother, pay attention, I beg you. You say to me: Why are you seeking me? I answer: Because you are my brother. You answer me and say: If I have perished, why are you seeking me? And I answer: If you had not perished, I would not be seeking you. Why are you seeking me? You say to me: If I have perished, why are you seeking me? When I answer: I am seeking you because you have perished. And why am I seeking you, for what gain? So that one day it may be said to me: Your brother was dead and has come to life again; he had perished and has been found. You answer me and say: But I have the sacrament. You do have it; I acknowledge that. That is why I am seeking you. You have given me a great reason to seek you all the more diligently. For you are a sheep from my Lord's flock; you have strayed with the sign. That is why I seek you more, because you have the sign itself. Why do we not possess one church? We have one sign; why are we not in one sheepfold? I am seeking you so that this sacrament may be for you a help toward salvation, not a testimony toward condemnation. Do you not know that a deserter is condemned by the mark by which a soldier is honored? That is why I am seeking you, so that you may not perish with the sign. For it is a sign of salvation, if you have salvation, if you have love. This sign of salvation can be on you outwardly, but it cannot benefit you. Come, so that what you had may benefit you—not so that you may receive what you had, but so that what you had may begin to benefit you, and you may receive what you did not have. For you had the sign of peace, but you did not have peace itself. In that house—that is, in you—discord was living, and on the threshold it was posting signs of peace. I recognize the signs, but I am seeking the inhabitant. I read the sign of peace: baptism in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. It is a sign of peace; I read it. Who lives there, I am seeking. I look at my brother; I recognize the sign of peace. I too have it; I want to enter. What does 'I want to enter' mean? Accept me as your brother, so that together we may pray to the Father. 'I do not pray with you.' The signs of peace are there, and discord contradicts me? Clearly I will labor, with the Lord's help, to cast out discord, which possesses wrongly, and to bring in peace as the rightful possessor. So when I cast out discord and bring in peace, why should I take down the signs of peace? I say plainly to my Lord: O Christ, you who are our peace, who made both one—make us one, so that we may rightly sing: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell in unity. Bring in concord, drive out discord; bring in yourself into your own signs. You remain; let no other possess them and deceive by your signs.

problems.quote: This sign of salvation can be in you from outside
problems.source_quote: hoc enim signum salutis extra tibi inesse potest
problems.why: 'Extra' modifies the sign's location relative to the person (outside/externally present), not 'from outside' as source. Augustine means the sign can be present in you as something external (not inwardly effective), not that it comes from an external source.
problems.fix: This sign of salvation can be present in you externally

edits.old: This sign of salvation can be in you from outside
edits.new: This sign of salvation can be present in you externally

fixed: Corrected 'from outside' to 'externally': source 'extra tibi inesse potest' means the sign can be present in you as something external, not that it comes from an external source.

problems.quote: This sign of salvation can be present in you externally
problems.source_quote: hoc enim signum salutis extra tibi inesse potest
problems.why: 'Extra' = 'outside,' not 'externally in you.' The paradox is: the sign can be outside you (i.e., on you but not within/saving you), not 'present in you externally.' Augustine says it can be on you outwardly but not inwardly effective.
problems.fix: This sign of salvation can be on you outwardly
problems.ruling: 'extra tibi inesse' means 'be in you outside' (outwardly); 'present in you externally' garbs the paradox.

edits.old: This sign of salvation can be present in you externally
edits.new: This sign of salvation can be on you outwardly

fixed: Changed 'present in you externally' to 'on you outwardly' because 'extra' means 'outside,' and the point is that the sign can be on a person outwardly without being inwardly effective.

last_rejected.quote: you have strayed with the sign
last_rejected.why: Latin 'cum' means 'with' as accompaniment/instrument, not 'while carrying'; the sheep strayed and the sign went with it, but 'with' in English suggests the sign caused or accompanied the straying. Better: 'you have strayed bearing the mark' or 'marked, you have strayed.'
last_rejected.fix: you have strayed bearing the mark
last_rejected.ruling: 'cum signo errasti' = 'you strayed with the sign.' English 'with' correctly renders accompaniment. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: a deserter is condemned by the mark by which a soldier is honored
last_rejected.source_quote: desertor de charactere damnatur, de quo militans honoratur
last_rejected.why: Latin 'de' means 'on account of' or 'because of,' not instrumental 'by.' The deserter is condemned *because of* the mark (for deserting despite having it), while the soldier is honored *because of* it. English 'by' suggests agency/means, flipping the sense to 'condemned through the instrument of the mark.'
last_rejected.fix: a deserter is condemned on account of the mark for which a soldier is honored
last_rejected.ruling: 'de charactere damnatur' = 'condemned by the mark.' 'By' correctly renders agency/means. Mere preference for 'because of.'

last_rejected.quote: This sign of salvation can be on you outwardly, but it cannot benefit you
last_rejected.source_quote: hoc enim signum salutis extra tibi inesse potest, prodesse non potest
last_rejected.why: 'extra' means 'outside' (i.e., external to you, not inwardly possessed/efficacious), not 'outwardly' (which suggests visible vs. invisible). The contrast is external possession vs. internal profit, not outward appearance.
last_rejected.fix: This sign of salvation can be outside you, but it cannot benefit you
last_rejected.ruling: 'extra tibi inesse' = 'be in you outwardly/externally.' 'Outwardly' is within normal range. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: not so that you may receive what you had
last_rejected.why: The Latin says 'not so that you may receive what you had'—but this is paradoxical since he already has it. The English should preserve this paradox: he doesn't come to *receive* what he *had* (already possesses), but so it may begin to profit him. The 'had' is key—he already possesses it.
last_rejected.fix: not so that you may receive what you already had
last_rejected.ruling: English exactly matches source: 'non ut accipias quod habebas' = 'not so that you may receive what you had.' No error.

last_rejected.quote: on the threshold it was posting signs of peace
last_rejected.why: The subject is discord ('discordia'), which is personified as posting signs of peace on the threshold. English 'it was posting' loses the personification and makes the grammar unclear. 'Discord' should be the explicit subject.
last_rejected.fix: discord was posting signs of peace on the threshold
last_rejected.ruling: 'it was posting' correctly refers to 'discordia' (preceding clause). Personification preserved. Mere preference.

last_rejected.why: This is Augustine speaking, continuing from 'ipsum et ego habeo'—'I too have it; I want to enter [the house, i.e., the person].' But the English makes it sound like a new voice or a quotation. The context shows Augustine is speaking of entering the 'house' where discord dwells, to cast it out.
last_rejected.ruling: 'intrare uolo' = 'I want to enter.' Accurate. Context makes clear Augustine is speaker. Mere preference.

last_rejected.why: The Latin imperative 'accipe' is Augustine's words to the 'inhabitant' (peace/Christ), not to the brother. He wants to enter so that peace may receive him as brother. The English 'Accept me as your brother' without clear addressee makes it seem like Augustine addresses Emeritus, but he's addressing the absent peace/Christ.
last_rejected.ruling: 'fratrem me accipe' = 'Accept me as your brother.' Accurate literal translation. Addressee ambiguity exists in Latin too. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: The signs of peace are there, and discord contradicts me?
last_rejected.source_quote: tituli pacis sunt, et mihi discordia contradicit?
last_rejected.why: 'sunt' here means 'they are present/exist' or 'are mine too'—Augustine has the same signs. 'Et mihi' means 'even to me' or 'me too'—discord contradicts him (Augustine) as well? Or: 'I too have the signs of peace, so does discord contradict me?' The English loses the sense that Augustine also possesses these signs.
last_rejected.fix: I too have the signs of peace, so does discord contradict me?
last_rejected.ruling: 'tituli pacis sunt' = 'the signs of peace are there.' 'Sunt' = exist/are present. 'Et mihi' = 'and to me.' Reasonable rendering. Mere preference.

last_rejected.why: 'Male' means 'wickedly' or 'evilly,' not 'wrongly' (which suggests incorrectness rather than moral evil). Discord is an evil usurper, not merely mistaken.
last_rejected.ruling: 'male possidentem' = 'possesses wrongly/wickedly.' 'Wrongly' is within normal range, includes moral sense. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: You remain; let no other possess them and deceive by your signs
last_rejected.source_quote: tu mane, non alter possideat et de titulis tuis fallat
last_rejected.why: 'Tu mane' is imperative: 'You remain/stay!' not indicative 'You remain.' Augustine is commanding Christ to remain in his signs. 'Non alter possideat' is 'let no other possess' but 'et de titulis tuis fallat' means 'and deceive by means of your signs'—the usurper deceives others using Christ's signs.
last_rejected.fix: You, remain; let no other possess and deceive by your signs
last_rejected.ruling: 'tu mane' = 'You remain' (imperative). English 'You remain' can be imperative. 'De titulis tuis fallat' = 'deceive by your signs.' Accurate.
